I farm 200 mu, so I do not plan like a small household plot. I will keep the land in crops that give me stable output first, then I will leave a smaller share for the higher-labor crop. For Quzhou, wheat and maize are still my backbone because they fit the land, the water, and the machinery work. I have well irrigation, so I will not be stingy on water at the key stages. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield from weak growth. I will also separate the fields by crop strength: squash goes on the better, flatter, easier-watered land because it needs tighter management and more spraying; millet goes on the lighter ground because it handles stress better and does not need as much fertilizer as maize or squash. With my years in the field, I do not just copy last year blindly, but I still start from the rates that already worked and then adjust by crop demand. This year I will use hybrid maize and squash seed, improved wheat and millet seed, keep wheat and maize as the main volume crops, and push potassium harder on squash because fruiting crops pull a lot. On 200 mu, efficiency matters, so I will mostly use rotary tillage where it saves time, but I will plough the squash ground because I want deeper loose soil and better manure and fertilizer mixing.
